mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for two consecutive months reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of expected corporate cash flows and thereby depressing S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the policy tightening period (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS decline is not sustained for ≥2 months.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment (UNRATE) below 4% for three consecutive months indicates a strengthening labor market, which increases consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% and remains below for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative despite UNRATE below 4% for the required period, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average signals accelerating economic demand, which elevates earnings expectations and pushes up S&P 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO crosses above 12-month moving average and remains above for 2 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the INDPRO expansion phase.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 3% for four consecutive months reduces policy uncertainty and supports investor optimism, producing positive S&P 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 3% and remains below for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite CPIAUCSL remaining below 3% for the required window.

mechanism_narrative: When the ratio of residential housing starts (HOUST) to prior month exceeds 1.05 for two consecutive months, it signals renewed construction activity, which lowers borrowing costs and supports equity valuations, pushing up S&P 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the housing start acceleration.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the monthly payrolls (PAYEMS) below the prior month accompanied by a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 4.5% indicates a labor market softening, which can depress earnings expectations and drive negative S&P 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the defined labor market cooling pattern.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive 2-month decline in consumer demand proxy (RSAFS) below 700 million suggests waning demand, which can lead to valuation adjustments and negative S&P 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls below 700 for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the decline in RSAFS.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls by more than 0.25 percentage points from its peak in the prior 12 months, it signals a prolonged easing phase that increases risk appetite and drives positive S&P 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the defined easing phase.
